name: Canopy-Deep
description: Canopy-Deep takes its name from the planet-spanning mat of floating vegetation that covers roughly seventy percent of its ocean surface, so dense and interwoven that it forms a canopy over the waters beneath. Sunlight filters through this living roof in dappled green patterns, creating an underworld of shadowed lagoons and root-tangled waterways. Where the canopy thins near the poles, open ocean reveals water so clear that the bioluminescent deep is visible from the surface, glowing like a submerged aurora.

Navigating Canopy-Deep's under-surface waterways feels like exploring a flooded forest. The roots of the floating canopy hang like curtains, draped with luminescent organisms, and the water carries the green scent of chlorophyll and the mineral tang of the geothermal vents that warm the polar seas. Sound travels strangely beneath the canopy, muffled and directionless, giving the space an intimate, enclosed quality unlike any open ocean.

The canopy mat has been growing continuously for an estimated sixty million years, and core samples reveal layers of compressed vegetation extending dozens of meters down, a floating geological record of the planet's biological history. Deep within these compressed layers, researchers have found crystallized organic compounds with no analogue in known biochemistry. The canopy appears to be slowly thickening, and models suggest it will achieve complete ocean coverage within the next million years, fundamentally transforming the planet's energy cycle.

Canopy-Deep's medicinal compounds, derived from organisms found only in the deepest root tangles, have proven effective against several previously untreatable neurological conditions. Harvesting requires specialized submersible equipment and carries significant risk, as the root systems respond to damage by releasing paralytic compounds into the surrounding water. The planet remains uncolonized, its value measured entirely in what can be carefully, painstakingly extracted from its living depths.
